note: Answer key for the anything-uxui eval harness. Every rule-id below exists verbatim as a heading in skills/anything-uxui/references/. Fixtures deliberately carry no rule-ids in their comments: naming the answer inside the fixture would contaminate the run.

scoring.hit: The expected rule-id string appears verbatim in the audit output.
scoring.verdict: The audit closes with the expected Block or Approve.
scoring.pass: ≥ 90% of expected rule-ids hit across all cases, every verdict correct, and no fix that breaks the component.
scoring.extraFindings: Additional rule-ids beyond the expected list are not counted as misses. On the control they are only acceptable while the verdict stays Approve.

addedIn.component-no-hover-grow: 3.1.0. The rule did not exist in 3.0.0, so the 3.0.0 baseline was scored over the other five ids only. The fixture has carried the hover scale-up since it was written (line 56, whileHover scale 1.05) and was not changed for this.

cases.breakage: framer-motion import, transition: all 300ms ease-in, no :active rule, 16px icon button, hover scale-up on a frequently pressed button
live region mounted together with its content, indicator shown with no delay window on a ~200ms fetch, 3 flat bars standing in for 64px avatar rows
Inter, blue-to-purple gradient on hero text and CTA, emoji atop three identical cards, badge plus centered hero scaffold
reorder reachable only by dragging: no move buttons, no keyboard path, no overflow menu
useOptimistic on a destructive invoice delete with no undo, no pending cue, and a silent rollback
none: this is the false-positive control. It encodes component-active-scale, easing-custom-curves, a11y-target-size-24, perf-transform-opacity-only, a gated hover and a reduced-motion fallback.

workflows.note: Fixtures for the three workflows added in 3.1.0. These are not run by the 3.0.0 baseline: the commands do not exist yet.

expectSuggested.why: a pressable element with hover and focus styling but no press feedback
an occasionally-seen surface that currently appears with a hard cut

expectRejected.why: opened with Cmd+K many times a day, so the gate must reject it on frequency and its keyboard trigger, and it must appear in the rejected-candidates section rather than being silently dropped

animate.request: add an open/close animation to the command palette
animate.why: the correct answer is to build nothing: the palette is a high-frequency keyboard-triggered surface, so the gate must stop before any code is written

plan.targetNote: the folder holding the 6 audit cases
motionPlansAlsoContain: an exact cubic-bezier (literal, or a token whose literal is defined in a plan it declares as a dependency)
